answer: Agents tracking raven flocks across open tundra can resist Sybil attacks via bidirectional optical beam-sectoring at relay masts. In a brief epoch, each mast directs a narrow laser pulse carrying a nonce into fixed angular sectors and admits one signed optical reply per sector. Because simultaneous sector locks block time-sharing one unit, attackers must field and power separate spaced transceivers per identity, though blowing snow can scatter beams and lock out honest nodes.
